newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech gov't calls 20 min recess for talks with MP.
newsitem.headline: Czech gov't calls 20 min recess for talks with MP.

text.p: Government parties have called a 20 minute recess just ahead of a confidence vote to hold further talks with independent Member of Parliament Jozef Wagner.

Parliament was scheduled to begin voting when Wagner spoke to deputies asking the government to allow parliament to vote on banking privatisation, a condition which he set in exchange for his support.
Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus earlier rejected this demand.
The hastily called recess came after a Communist deputy, Miroslav Vacek, who was not expected to vote because of illness arrived at parliament.
With Vacek present, the government must rely on one opposition or independent deputy to vote with it to gain the required simple majority of members present.
Klaus's three-party, centre-right coalition controls only 100 seats in the 200-seat parliament.
Klaus rejected Wagner's proposal earlier, saying the cabinet would inform the lower house of its privatisation plans, but the sales were "an act of an executive type" and "not a task" for parliament.
Klaus called for the vote of confidence in his embattled cabinet and its programme aimed at answering an economic downturn and crisis in confidence in the Czech crown.
